rules.title: Criminal Background Check and Arrest Record Limitations
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from using blanket bans on applicants with a criminal record or considering arrests without convictions during tenant screening.

coverage.summary: Applies to residential rental properties subject to California fair housing laws.

rules.quoted_span: Blanket bans on applicants with a criminal record are prohibited, as are policies that consider arrests without convictions.

rules.title: Source of Income Protection for Section 8 Vouchers
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from refusing to participate in government housing subsidy programs like Section 8, making 'No Section 8' policies illegal.

coverage.summary: Applies broadly to housing providers under the Fair Employment and Housing Act.

rules.quoted_span: In 2019, the California Legislature adopted SB 329 , which updated the definition of “source of income” used in the Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) to include government housing subsidy programs, such as Section 8.

rules.title: Credit History Restrictions for Subsidy Recipients
rules.requirement: Rental property owners are prohibited from using an applicant's credit history as part of the application process if they have a government rental subsidy, unless they offer the option to provide alternative evidence of a verifiable legal means to pay rent.

coverage.summary: Applies to applicants with government rental subsidies.

rules.quoted_span: In addition, last year’s SB 267 amended FEHA to prohibit rental property owners from using a person’s credit history as part of the application process – if they have a government rental subsidy, such as Section 8 — without offering the applicant the option to provide alternative evidence of a verifiable legal means to pay their portion of the rent.
